line.comment: * Task 0.
* "Cartographer".
* We create a special array to handle explorer sync, for performance purposes. See Mayhem.GetExplorers.
* From Mayhem FoF:
* Filled by the CheckAttacked: and CheckAvoid: subroutines at the foot of the file and read by the
* main loop above them. They are initialized here because the compiler's unassigned-variable check
* reads the file in order, and a variable assigned only inside a gosub trips it.
* The sector this ship has taken from the homebase list and not yet put a satellite in.
* Zero Hour: hard difficulty allows Explorers to claim empty sectors
* Zero Hour: hard and insane difficulty allow Explorers to claim empty sectors
* ZH 1.8: only 2% chance for such opportunistic claims
* ZH 2.0: reduced further to 0.2% but its no longer limited to the earlygame
* Add-Ons 1.3: Chance increased to 1% on insane.
* Sector is Unknown
* An interrupted claim must not be completed after an emergency retreat.
* Once there we need to check again because we didn't already claim on departure like Battlegroups do
* Mordan9
* If the factory was destroyed or the explorer was reassigned, restart immediately.
* Same homebase, has no eligible sector.
* Do not continue a suspended mapping destination after an attack.
* The sector may have changed owner, blacklist status, or satellite coverage during travel.
* From FoF: 2026-08-20 The satellite goes down the moment the ship arrives.
* Drop a satellite and set it to be owned by the player if this is the NPC doing us a favor.
* Only NOW ask whether to stay.
* Leaving from here costs the trip nothing, because the sector is already mapped and the ship is still standing on the gate it arrived by.
* Actual attack: let ResolveRetreat handle the escape.
* Hostile presence without fire: select another mapping target.
* $underAttack means leave.
* $underFire distinguishes an actual attack from the presence of hostile armed ships.
* Plot exemptions. Only Phanon and player are possible.
* Expanded 2.2.1: Presence is actionable only for genuinely hostile, armed ships.
* Freighters are non-aggressors; defensive armament alone is not a threat.
* End enemy check.
* Leaving is the caller's job, and $underFire decides whether that is home or the next target on
* the list. This records why, tells the
* player, and remembers the sector so the next selection pass does not send the ship straight back.
* The memory is a per-ship local: it dies with the explorer and touches no global, no menu and
* nobody else's routing.
* $avoidSector is supplied by the caller.
* Half an hour of playing time, then the sector is fair game again -- long enough that the explorer
* gets useful work done elsewhere in the meantime, short enough that a garrison the player has
* since cleared out does not stay off the map forever. The entry is removed as it expires, so the
* table cannot grow without bound.
* Whether $sector still wants a satellite from this owner. It is asked when the list is built and
* again as each sector is taken, because the list can be minutes old by then.
* For the AI, we manage sector blacklist here.
* already handled by Zero Hour Core AI update
* No second satellite where we already have one.
* Only one explorer rebuilds the list at a time, because a second rebuild would put back sectors
* already taken. The marker counts only while its ship still exists and is still exploring.
* As such, one left by a destroyed or reassigned explorer is cleared.
* Every sector in reach that still wants a satellite, except the one each other explorer from this homebase is flying to right now.
* The wait is what spreads this loop's cost over time
* The homebase list of sectors waiting for a satellite, shared by every explorer based there.
* A sector leaves the list in the same instant it is taken, so no two explorers are sent to the same
* one, and the list is rebuilt only once it is empty. Returns $sector, or null when nothing is left that this ship may take.
* The homebase may have changed while we waited.
* A ship that has just waited on a rebuild, or run one, takes the empty list as the answer.
* The nearest sector to where this ship is now, passing over any it was recently driven out of.
* Off the list and onto this ship with no wait in between, so no other explorer can take it.
* A sector that has gained a satellite or turned hostile since the list was built is dropped,
* and the next nearest taken instead.
* Defer servicing while emergency retreat is pending.
* $t = [THIS] + ' in ' + [SECTOR] + ' has stopped working.'
* START [NULL]-> call script 'Joubarbe.Lib.Infobox': text=$t icon=29 timeout=0 fadeout=0
* Remember where the attack began.
* The previous mapping assignment is no longer valid.
* Limit immediate escape attempts to avoid tight retry loops.
* The explorer must have left the attacked sector.
* Any new sector must also be free of actionable threats.
* No longer under attack. Consume the retreat state.
* This sector is still dangerous. Avoid it on future visits.
* Select a new destination from the current position.
* Homebase is the last destination fallback.
* No route can currently be taken.
* Check the result of the final attempt.
* Unresolved: preserve the marker and retry after a delay.
* Do not resume normal mapping in a dangerous sector.
